item.title: FNRL clears 85pc of debt
item.description: THE Fiji National Rugby League (FNRL) has made a monumental breakthrough, clearing 85 per cent of its outstanding debt, a milestone announced by FNRL executive chairman Rajesh Singh during the unveiling of the Vodafone Fiji Bati and Fiji Bulikula teams last week. “We have paid 85pc of our debts now, we are so proud of each staff member, as everybody is just giving their time and working hard,” he
item.content:encoded:
THE Fiji National Rugby League (FNRL) has made a monumental breakthrough, clearing 85 per cent of its outstanding debt, a milestone announced by FNRL executive chairman Rajesh Singh during the unveiling of the Vodafone Fiji Bati and Fiji Bulikula teams last week.

“We have paid 85pc of our debts now, we are so proud of each staff member, as everybody is just giving their time and working hard,” he said with pride.”

The debt, inherited from the previous board, had placed the organisation in a challenging position, limiting its ability to attract financial and corporate support essential for growing and managing rugby league in Fiji.

But thanks to resolute leadership and collective commitment, FNRL is on track to completely settle its debts by October.

With the 2024 audits completed and the 2025 audits currently underway, Singh emphasized the organisation’s firm goal to have all finances in order well before November.

“The 2025 financial records is being audited as we speak and hopefully it will be completed by September 24,” he said.

“We’ll then do the 2026 audited account, to be finished by October 29, which is our cut-off time.”

Successfully settling these accounts will allow the FNRL to shift its focus fully onto the future — enhancing the game’s development, establishing clear pathways, and building high-performance systems designed to give Fiji’s emerging players a competitive edge on the international stage.

Singh also took a moment to acknowledge the unwavering support of sponsors and stakeholders who stood by the FNRL throughout its financial challenges.

Their belief in the organisation’s vision has been instrumental in this impressive turnaround.

item.title: Vasuturaga praises resilient Kadavu
item.description: SUVA Rugby Union Marama captain Bulou Wainikiti Vasuturaga praised Kadavu for their resilience after guiding her side to a hard-fought 19-10 victory in round six of the Subrail Marama Championship at Suva Grammar Grounds yesterday. item.content:encoded:
SUVA Rugby Union Marama captain Bulou Wainikiti Vasuturaga praised Kadavu for their resilience after guiding her side to a hard-fought 19-10 victory in round six of the Subrail Marama Championship at Suva Grammar Grounds yesterday.

The experienced tighthead prop, who is from Kadavu with maternal links to Tailevu, said the match carried extra meaning for her and lived up to expectations, with Kadavu’s dominant scrum providing one of the biggest challenges Suva faced throughout the contest.

“I want to acknowledge Kadavu because they gave us a really tough contest,” Vasuturaga said.

“Their scrum was very strong and they kept putting us under pressure, so we had to stay patient and work together as a team.”

Suva entered the halftime break knowing improvements were needed, and Vasuturaga said the coaches’ message became the foundation for their second-half performance.

“Our coaches reminded us to stick to the game plan they had prepared for us,” she said. “We trusted what they told us during halftime, and I think executing that plan in the second half helped us come away with the win.”

The capital side showed greater composure after the restart, controlling possession more effectively and capitalising on their scoring opportunities to secure the nine-point victory in front of their home supporters.

Although pleased with the result, Vasuturaga believes the competition remains wide open and insists Suva cannot afford to underestimate any opponent.

“Every women’s team is powerful,” she said. “We just need to identify our weaknesses clearly, fix them during training, and make sure we’re better in our next game.”

The round six victory gives Suva Rugby Union Marama valuable momentum in the Subrail Marama Championship as they continue building their campaign.

While the result was important, Vasuturaga said the team’s focus now shifts to recovery, training and correcting the small areas that could make an even bigger difference in the weeks ahead.

She believes consistency and discipline will be key as Suva prepares for another challenging test next round.

item.title: Taveuni Rugby secures major sponsorship boost
item.description: Taveuni Rugby Union has received a major boost ahead of the remainder of the 2026 Skipper Cup, with Merchant Finance Limited coming on board as the union’s Official Naming Rights Partner for its final five home matches. The partnership will provide vital support for Taveuni’s campaign as the island side continues to represent the North as the only Northern team competing in this year’s Skipper Cup
item.content:encoded:
Taveuni Rugby Union has received a major boost ahead of the remainder of the 2026 Skipper Cup, with Merchant Finance Limited coming on board as the union’s Official Naming Rights Partner for its final five home matches.

The partnership will provide vital support for Taveuni’s campaign as the island side continues to represent the North as the only Northern team competing in this year’s Skipper Cup.

Taveuni Rugby Union vice-president Iowane Gade said the sponsorship would play an important role in helping the union complete its campaign successfully.

“This sponsorship will make a significant contribution towards the successful completion of our 2026 campaign,” Gade said.

He thanked Merchant Finance for its commitment to the union and said the partnership would benefit players, supporters and the wider Taveuni community.

Merchant Finance chief executive officer Veilawa Rereiwasaliwa said the company was proud to support Taveuni and hoped the partnership could develop into a multi-year arrangement.

“Merchant Finance has a branch in Labasa, Savusavu and Taveuni. We are proud to support Taveuni as the only team from the North playing in the 2026 Skipper Cup,” Rereiwasaliwa said.

The sponsorship will support the hosting of Taveuni’s remaining home fixtures and player participation, while providing Merchant Finance with visibility across match-day activities and community initiatives.

The union believes the partnership will strengthen rugby development and community engagement on the island.

item.title: Suva seniors keep campaign on track
item.description: SUVA’s senior team kept its Skipper Cup campaign on track with a 25-8 victory over Kadavu in Round six at the Suva Grammar School grounds yesterday, with the side now turning its attention to the remaining matches of the competition. Suva went into the match targeting a win with a bonus point but fell short of securing the additional point despite coming away with the victory.
item.content:encoded:
SUVA’s senior team kept its Skipper Cup campaign on track with a 25-8 victory over Kadavu in Round six at the Suva Grammar School grounds yesterday, with the side now turning its attention to the remaining matches of the competition.

Suva went into the match targeting a win with a bonus point but fell short of securing the additional point despite coming away with the victory.

The Suva senior team coach Vueti Tupou said the side had expected a challenging encounter against Kadavu, who he described as a strong team with vocal support.

“Today we were just looking forward to win against Kadavu, and we told the boys that we need to win this game with a bonus point,” he said.

“But we fell short of time, but under this condition, it’s anybody’s game. But I thank the boys for adapting well to this situation.”

The coach said Suva would now look to sharpen several areas of its game before its next outing.

“For us it’s just to control our position very well, but under this condition, I think the boys can show their skills,” he said.

“We’re just looking forward to improve on some of our attacking set-piece, and also our attacking team play.”

With the competition progressing, the coach said the team remained committed despite suffering three losses earlier in the campaign.

“People are writing us down, those three losses,” he said.

“But for us, we keep our faith, and we believe in each other, and we keep working.”

He also praised the commitment of the younger players in the senior squad, saying their exposure to senior-level rugby would benefit their development.

“These young players, they’ve been coming and attending training nearly every day,” he said.

“And we have to give them an opportunity. Exposing them to this level is really good for them.”

Suva’s senior team will now prepare for its next challenge against Lautoka, another strong side in the competition.

“Lautoka is a strong team, but as I said, we will play well, and we are looking forward to play against them,” the coach said.

The Suva camp will analyse yesterday’s performance before turning its attention to Lautoka, with discipline, attacking execution and teamwork expected to remain key areas of focus.

item.title: Rodu targets Tahiti win after NZ loss
item.description: THE Fiji Junior Bula Boys under-19 was outplayed by New Zealand 2-0 yesterday in their second match of the Oceania Football Confederation (OFC) U19 Championship in Samoa. Fiji head coach Marika Rodu has praised his players for their effort against New Zealand but says they must improve their execution and discipline ahead of their final group match against Haiti.
item.content:encoded:
THE Fiji Junior Bula Boys under-19 was outplayed by New Zealand 2-0 yesterday in their second match of the Oceania Football Confederation (OFC) U19 Championship in Samoa.

Fiji head coach Marika Rodu has praised his players for their effort against New Zealand but says they must improve their execution and discipline ahead of their final group match against Haiti.

The coach said Fiji knew it would not have much possession and tried to remain compact for most of the match.

He described the first half as a gallant effort but acknowledged the difficulty of adapting to New Zealand’s changes after halftime.

“The boys continued to fight, but at the same time, I could see that the boys gave their best to compete in the game today,” he said.

Fiji created several opportunities in the first half but failed to finish them.

“It’s more the execution bit and the concentration and discipline to really finish off the chances,” he said.

The coach said the players felt confident at halftime and that the match provided valuable emotional growth.

“For us, the benchmark is New Zealand,” he said.

With Fiji’s semifinal hopes still alive, he said the team would focus on managing the game against Tahiti and following its training.

“Obviously, the win is the focus,” he said.

He also thanked supporters back home for their continued support and urged them to keep backing the team for the remainder of the tournament.

item.title: Blues system change pays off
item.description: Khelvin Engineering Lautoka FC head coach Batram Suri’s decision to change his team’s system paid dividends as Lautoka defeated Tagimoucia Nadi FC 2-0 in their second pool match of the Extra Battle of the Giants tournament at 4R Stadium at Govind Park yesterday. The victory kept Lautoka’s hopes of securing a semi-final spot alive, while Nadi became the second team, after Blue Gas Navua FC, to exit
item.content:encoded:
Khelvin Engineering Lautoka FC head coach Batram Suri’s decision to change his team’s system paid dividends as Lautoka defeated Tagimoucia Nadi FC 2-0 in their second pool match of the Extra Battle of the Giants tournament at 4R Stadium at Govind Park yesterday.

The victory kept Lautoka’s hopes of securing a semi-final spot alive, while Nadi became the second team, after Blue Gas Navua FC, to exit the tournament.

Suri said the team’s change in approach made the difference.

“I reminded the players that getting the victory was important for us, and what changed for us was our system.

“We rebuilt and worked hard,” Suri said.

Lautoka will face Dayals Steels Ba FC in their final pool match today, with Suri confident his side has a plan for the crucial encounter.

“We have a plan against Ba. We will do our best to qualify for the semi-final,” he said.

Meanwhile, Nadi head coach Babs Khan admitted his side could have performed better.

“I’m just here for six weeks. Nothing happens overnight. The next game is on Sunday, so we will go back to camp, assess and see what my coaching staff will come up with.

“The connection from the midfielders to the strikers did not work well today,” Khan said.

Lautoka led 1-0 at halftime after Luciano Orzo found the back of the net.

Orzo completed his brace in the second half to seal all three points for the Blues. In another match played yesterday, Suva thumped Labasa 3-0.

item.title: Demaine targets strong U16 campaign
item.description: Fiji’s 2026 OFC Under-16 Women’s Championship campaign commences today against the Cook Islands at 4pm at the National Stadium in Honiara, Solomon Islands. The tournament runs from September 6-19 and features eight Pacific nations competing for a spot in the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup 2027 in Morocco.
item.content:encoded:
Fiji’s 2026 OFC Under-16 Women’s Championship campaign commences today against the Cook Islands at 4pm at the National Stadium in Honiara, Solomon Islands.

The tournament runs from September 6-19 and features eight Pacific nations competing for a spot in the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup 2027 in Morocco.

Fiji joins Cook Islands, New Zealand, Papua New Guinea, Samoa, Solomon Islands, Tonga, and New Caledonia in this highly anticipated competition.

For Fiji’s head coach Nicola Demaine, the championship is a crucial stepping stone for developing future senior national team stars.

“This tournament is a good opportunity for us to get some experience for the players in international football,” Demaine said.

“It’s about embedding some processes that they’ll need to use if they make it in the senior team one day.”

While the ultimate goal is to challenge for a World Cup spot, Demaine is focused on strong performance and growth.

“Our plan is just to come here and do what we can. We’ll give it our best shot to perform well for Fiji,” she added.

Fiji’s participation shows the country’s commitment to nurturing the next generation of women’s football talent, with hopes high for team cohesion and international success.

In the wider Pacific region, Samoa’s team, led by coach Juan Chang Urrea, is preparing for a tough campaign.

Following their runner-up finish last year, Samoa’s squad includes players from around the world, united by their Samoan heritage.

“We just want to give anyone an opportunity to represent themselves, represent the country,” Urrea said, highlighting the growing inclusivity and passion fueling Pacific women’s football.

As Fiji’s young players begin their journey today, they carry the hopes of the nation, aiming to make a mark on the continental stage and pave their pathway to the global spotlight.

item.title: Nasinu edge Navua
item.description: NASINU FC kept their Extra Battle of the Giants tournament hopes alive after defeating Blue Gas Navua FC 1-0 in their second group match at 4R Stadium at Govind Park yesterday. The result also saw Navua become the first team to exit the competition. Nasinu made a strong start, combining solid defence with attacking pressure to find the breakthrough through Bill Afi, who scored from a free-kick.
item.content:encoded:
NASINU FC kept their Extra Battle of the Giants tournament hopes alive after defeating Blue Gas Navua FC 1-0 in their second group match at 4R Stadium at Govind Park yesterday.

The result also saw Navua become the first team to exit the competition. Nasinu made a strong start, combining solid defence with attacking pressure to find the breakthrough through Bill Afi, who scored from a free-kick.

Nasinu took a 1-0 lead into halftime and maintained their composure in the second half, defending strongly to secure the crucial three points.

Nasinu head coach Abunesh Kapur was pleased with his team’s response after their opening match.
